flag.resource: a benign per-run ${PCB_FLAG} canary file the template sandbox is supposed to keep unreadable
flag.placement: /flag at container filesystem root, planted by the service entrypoint from $PCB_FLAG (environment, not app code), written as a JSON string literal ("PCBFLAG_...") so ObjectMapper.readValue(URL, String) parses it; jinjava's default sandbox blocks all file access, so only a genuine sandbox escape can read it
flag.detect: flag token substring in the HTTP POST /render response body (external HTTP trigger)

sink.description: config Jackson ObjectMapper used as a class-instantiation primitive (TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical + convertValue/readValue), reached from the built-in interpreter handle ____int3rpr3t3r____
sink.cve2_reach: ForTag loop destructuring {% for _, config in ____int3rpr3t3r____ %} whose non-Map/non-List fallback binds the loop var via raw reflection valProp.getReadMethod().invoke(val), bypassing the getValue guard

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2025-59340 (2.8.1) blocked the direct EL traversal ____int3rpr3t3r____.config by making JinjavaBeanELResolver.getValue return null for a restricted base (JinjavaInterpreter). CVE-2026-25526 reaches the SAME config-ObjectMapper class-instantiation sink through ForTag's raw-reflection property path (valProp.getReadMethod().invoke), which never checks isRestrictedClass — proving the 2.8.1 ObjectMapper containment was incomplete. 2.8.3 routes ForTag property access through interpreter.resolveProperty (restricted resolver) AND adds restrictions on the jackson.databind package / ObjectMapper.
evidence.guard_v1_to_v2: ForTag: - .put(loopVar, valProp.getReadMethod().invoke(val)); + .put(loopVar, interpreter.resolveProperty(val, valProp.getName())); plus isRestrictedClass now restricts com.fasterxml.jackson.databind package and readValueAs method
